purpose: Resolve the public Aurora cohort lineage as far as outcome-blind metadata permit and determine whether endpoint cadence or same-condition block size is the binding constraint on a future independent ordinal battery-lifetime test.
claimBoundary: RWTH cell outcomes were opened in RC55 and are used only as an empirical design prior. No Aurora BDF cycling row, cell capacity, or EOL value may be opened. A schedule that passes this contract is a prospective design, not validation of a lifetime coordinate.

lineageGate.paperCohort: The primary paper reports one 36-cell LFP/graphite batch in Figure 7.
lineageGate.requiredManifest: Before outcomes, one official machine-readable table must map all 36 paper-cohort members to unique cell IDs, assembly metadata, cycling protocol, and BDF entries.
lineageGate.roCrateTest: Inspect only ro-crate-metadata.json, the prior metadata-only RC56 audit, the ZIP central directory, and the Zenodo record. Inventory membership alone does not establish study-cohort membership.
lineageGate.pass: Exactly 36 unique cells are explicitly assigned to the Figure 7 LFP batch and each maps one-to-one to metadata, CSV, and Parquet entries.
lineageGate.fail: If chemistry or paper-cohort membership must be inferred from ID proximity, file order, aggregate counts, or cycling values, exclude Aurora from confirmatory testing.

pairDesign.latentCrossingProxy: For each of the 48 outcome-open RWTH cells, linearly interpolate cycle time only between the adjacent standardized capacity rounds bracketing 80% of its own BOL capacity. This proxy is used only to compare inspection designs.
pairDesign.featureRegister: Keep the candidate coordinate separate: BOL and standardized full-capacity checks nominally at cycles 160, 320, and 480; the frozen candidate is log(Q_R3/Q_R0).
pairDesign.endpointRegister: After nominal cycle 480, quantize the interpolated 80% crossing to a fixed grid. Candidate construction may not use the denser endpoint register.
pairDesign.spreadDefinition: Scale every empirical crossing deviation from the empirical median by the registered factor. The 0.25 case represents a future same-condition batch whose lifetime spread is only one quarter of RWTH's.
pairDesign.phaseRobustness: For each interval, evaluate every integer-cycle phase offset from zero through interval minus one and retain the worst phase.
pairDesign.samplingDistribution: Draw future event times with replacement from the 48 transformed empirical crossings. Compute the multinomial pair-count distribution exactly; no Monte Carlo random numbers are used.
pairDesign.pairDefinition: Count only non-tied event-event pairs inside one same-condition block. This is conservative with respect to usable event-censor pairs.
pairDesign.gate: At the 0.25 spread scale and worst grid phase, require both exact P(non-tied pairs >= 100) >= 0.95 and the lower 5% pair-count quantile >= 100.
pairDesign.selection: For each effective event count, select the largest tested interval that passes every gate. The principal design must also preserve at least 24 independently observed events.
pairDesign.prohibited: Do not weaken the 100-pair gate, choose a favorable grid phase, count cross-condition pairs, treat interpolated crossings as validation outcomes, or inspect Aurora cycling data.

measurementIntervention.risk: A denser reference-performance-test schedule can change calendar time, thermal history, rest, and charge throughput and therefore can change the degradation process it is meant to observe.
measurementIntervention.control: All confirmatory cells receive the same frozen schedule and channel-randomization plan. A separate non-confirmatory pilot must compare dense and conventional schedules before claiming transport.
measurementIntervention.adaptiveBranch: A capacity-loss-triggered RPT schedule is retained as a later burden-reduction hypothesis, not substituted for the fixed-grid decisive test until trigger sensitivity and intervention equivalence are independently established.

decisionRule: Aurora is eligible only if the lineage gate passes. A future experiment is pair-powered only if the exact worst-phase design gate passes. Failure of either gate keeps target outcomes closed and prevents a transport claim.
safetyAndScope: This cycle performs public metadata inspection and offline computation only. Physical cycling would require an approved laboratory protocol, temperature and voltage protection, calibrated channels, and a predefined response to swelling, leakage, venting, or thermal excursion. No cyber-trust work is included.
